Categories.value: Enchey Monastery|Self-published work|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2022 in India|Indian monuments with Wikidata QIDs|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Files from competitions organized by West Bengal Wikimedians User Group|Uploaded via Campaign:wlm-in-sk|India photographs taken on 2021-10-15|Images from Wiki Loves Monuments 2022|Images from WLM 2022 India under review by Montage tool

ImageDescription.value: Enchey Monastery of Gangtok, India belongs to the Nyingma order of Vajrayana Buddhism and falls under the jurisdiction of the Pemayangtse Monastery. Enchey means "Solitary" and as its name implies, the monastery has a very peaceful atmosphere. The monastery was built in 1909 resembling a Chinese Pagoda, with ornately carved windows and a shining golden cupola on top. On a clear day, the Kanchendzonga range is visible from the monastery which is built on a ridge above Gangtok city. It is the exact location where Lama Druptub Karbo had his hermitage. The photograph was taken in the late afternoon of October 2021.
